doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Faking terrible Japanese jazz records
summary: Mandel says he duplicated the awful style rather than using real records, telling players to play their own style and sometimes writing in 6/8.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: He said, “Can you make the records that bad?” I said, “Don’t worry, we can make them rotten.”
So, well, for those things did you get authentic Japanese 1949 jazz records or you just try to duplicate that feel?
I duplicated the feel, but I knew how to do it.
What did you tell the players?
I played them a little of it and I said, “Play your own style.” [laughs]
Kind of like, Jonathan and Darlene Edwards. [A Jo Stafford, Paul Weston comedy album]
That’s right, it was. You know, I said, “Don’t try to be funny, just play it like this.”
Sometimes we’d actually write it in 6/8 too, to get that feel.
